desc: Mammoth Cave in Kentucky is the longest known cave system in the world, with over 675 km of surveyed passageways. Established as Mammoth Cave National Park in 1941, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and an International Biosphere Reserve. The cave system formed in Mississippian-aged limestone strata and features massive chambers, underground rivers, and unique cave-dwelling species. The cave has been known to Native Americans for thousands of years and was extensively explored and commercialized in the 19th century. It is home to over 130 species of wildlife adapted to darkness including eyeless fish and cave crickets.
fact: It is the longest known cave system in the world with over 675 km of passages · It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and Biosphere Reserve · It features massive chambers and underground rivers in limestone strata · It is home to over 130 species of cave-adapted wildlife

desc: The Waitomo Glowworm Caves are a famous cave system in the Waikato region of New Zealand's North Island. The caves are renowned for their population of glowworms (Arachnocampa luminosa), which create a spectacular bioluminescent display on the cave ceilings. The limestone caves were formed over 30 million years ago and feature impressive stalactites, stalagmites, and underground rivers. The caves were first explored by local Māori chief Tane Tinorau in 1887. Visitors can take boat tours through the glowworm grotto. The surrounding area has a network of over 300 known cave systems.
fact: The Waitomo caves are famous for spectacular bioluminescent glowworms on the ceilings · The limestone caves formed over 30 million years ago · They were first explored by Māori chief Tane Tinorau in 1887 · Surrounding area has over 300 known cave systems

desc: Son Doong Cave in Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park, Vietnam, is the largest cave in the world by volume. Discovered in 1991 by a local man named Hồ Khanh and explored in 2009 by British cavers, the cave features a 5 km-long main passage with chambers up to 200 meters tall and 150 meters wide. The cave contains its own weather system, with clouds forming inside the massive chambers. It has its own jungle ecosystem (dolin) where sunlight enters through collapsed ceilings. The cave is traversed by a massive underground river. Its main chamber could fit a 40-story skyscraper.
fact: Son Doong is the largest cave in the world by volume · Main passage is 5 km long with chambers 200 meters tall · The cave has its own weather system with clouds forming inside · It contains an internal jungle ecosystem and a massive underground river

desc: Carlsbad Caverns National Park in New Mexico, USA, contains some of the largest and most spectacular limestone caves in the world. The main chamber, the Big Room, is the largest cave chamber in North America at over 1,200 meters long, 180 meters wide, and 75 meters high. The caves formed when sulfuric acid dissolved the surrounding limestone, creating unique formations including the famous Rock of Ages and the Giant Dome. The caves are famous for the evening flight of millions of Brazilian free-tailed bats from the entrance. The site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
fact: The Big Room is the largest cave chamber in North America · The caves formed uniquely through sulfuric acid dissolution of limestone · Millions of Brazilian free-tailed bats emerge from the entrance each evening · Carlsbad Caverns is a UNESCO World Heritage Site

desc: Postojna Cave is a 24 km-long karst cave system near Postojna, Slovenia, one of the most extensive cave systems in Europe. It is the second-longest cave system in Slovenia and a premier tourist attraction with a underground railway since 1872. The cave features spectacular stalagmite and stalactite formations, including the famous 5-meter tall 'Brilliant' formation. It is the type locality of the olm, the blind aquatic salamander known as the 'human fish.' Parts of the cave were formed by the Pivka River, which flows through the system. The cave has been visited by over 40 million people and has a unique subterranean ecosystem.
fact: Postojna Cave has a 24 km karst system with an underground railway since 1872 · It is the type locality of the olm, the blind 'human fish' salamander · The 'Brilliant' formation is a famous 5-meter stalagmite · Over 40 million people have visited the cave system
